meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (national-level incorporation; no separate provincial company registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system combining Roman-Dutch common law, English common law influence, African customary law, and constitutional supremacy
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Republic of South Africa and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income, signed 17 February 1997, as amended by the 2014 Protocol
Convention between South Africa and the United Kingdom for the Avoidance of Double Taxation, 2002
Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (South Africa ratified in 2018)
SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (2006)
Agreement Establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), 2018

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; Companies Act 71 of 2008; Companies Regulations, 2011 (GN R351 of 26 April 2011); Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 and Companies Second Amendment Act 17 of 2024, both effective 27 December 2024

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each proposed director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or Department of Home Affairs of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued by a public authority, or Consular Legalization through a South African embassy/consulate if the issuing state is not a member of the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address dated within 90 days of filing (utility bill, bank statement, or municipal account)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility company, bank, or municipal authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarisation followed by Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions; private documents require notarised certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate or certificate of good conduct for each foreign director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or ministry of justice of the country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization by a South African consular official if the issuing state is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account relationship, identity verification, source of funds, and absence of adverse AML/CDD findings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution or licensed bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarisation plus Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Pre-incorporation board or shareholder consent resolutions if executed outside South Africa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Accountable institutions under the FIC Act must identify and verify all clients and UBOs, determine whether any client or UBO is a domestic or foreign politically exposed person, including family members and close associates, and apply enhanced due diligence. Mandatory screening must cover the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, South African domestic designations under POCDATARA, and, where required by payment rails or correspondent banking, OFAC/EU/UK sanction lists and adverse-media alerts. Suspicious and unusual transactions must be reported to the Financial Intelligence Centre within 15 days; records must be retained for at least 5 years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-services Companies and Intellectual Property Commission online transaction system (https://eservices.cipc.co.za), Company Name Reservation and Registration module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Name applications must be submitted in Latin/alphabetical script; names in non-Latin scripts such as Chinese or Arabic must be transliterated into one of the 11 official languages of South Africa using Latin characters. The prescribed legal-form suffix '(Pty) Ltd' is mandatory, and punctuation is restricted to '&', '.', and '-'. A distinctive part is required to distinguish the name from existing registered names and trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where CIPC refuses a name reservation, the applicant receives a written notice specifying the ground of refusal, typically conflict with a pre-existing name or trademark, or use of a prohibited/sensitive token. The applicant may, before the expiry of the original reservation, apply once for an extension of 20 business days. On refusal, the applicant may: (a) resubmit Form CoR 9.1 with a modified distinctive part or with written consent from the holder of the conflicting name/trademark; (b) apply to the Companies Tribunal for reconsideration under section 160 of the Companies Act; or (c) seek judicial review under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000 in the High Court, ordinarily within 30 days of the refusal. An extension request must be lodged before the original reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for an automated dropshipping company provided the provider supplies a physical business address within South Africa that is capable of receiving service of legal process and statutory notices. The registered office may not be a post office box. A serviced or virtual office is acceptable where the company maintains its corporate records at that address and mail forwarding is provided.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a compliant non-licensed e-commerce shelf company, estimated at 5-10% per annum. If CIPC/FIC/SARS flags incomplete UBO declarations, cross-border payment anomalies, or a senior PEP as UBO, the probability of an unannounced physical verification rises to 25-40%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC name clearance reservation application (Form CoR 9.1), one name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff prescribed by the Companies Regulations, 2011, Schedule 1 (ZAR 50).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) and registration of a private company (Pty) Ltd
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed fee prescribed by the Companies Regulations, 2011, Schedule 1 (ZAR 175).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Attorney drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation, company rules, director declarations, and shareholder resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; typically ZAR 5,500-8,500 plus VAT for a standard single-shareholder proprietary limited company.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership register compilation and initial CIPC beneficial ownership filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Company secretarial service provider or attorney; CIPC if surcharge applies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; no separate CIPC statutory fee when filed at incorporation, but professional fee is typically ZAR 2,000-3,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarisation plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization for director/shareholder identity, address proof, police clearance, and bank reference (bundle of 3-4 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO), or South African consular office abroad
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee under the Legal Practice Act 28 of 2014 and government-gazetted DIRCO apostille fees, plus courier and translation-verification costs.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation and transliteration of non-English identity or corporate documents (estimated 3-5 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: South African certified or sworn translator, with notarial authentication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of approximately ZAR 350-550 per page.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical address / virtual office service for the first 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Serviced office or virtual office provider in South Africa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of ZAR 3,500-7,000 per annum for an e-commerce shelf company.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss. 11-14, 16, 19, 31, 36-40, 66, 69, 70, 93 and the Companies Regulations, 2011; ancillary application of the Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008 and the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 25 of 2002.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1) together with Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Proprietary Limited company; shares may be issued for any consideration determined by the board, subject to the solvency and liquidity test under s. 31 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. No mandatory escrow account is required by South African law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION: RESOLVED: (1) The Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation filed with CIPC are adopted and the date of incorporation is confirmed. (2) The share subscriptions in the initial share register are accepted; shares are issued upon receipt of subscribed capital. (3) The registered office address in the Notice of Incorporation is adopted for service of process and official correspondence. (4) The persons named in the director and officer register are appointed as directors, Company Secretary and financial officer, holding office until annual review. (5) The Company Secretary is authorised to complete all post-incorporation registrations, including tax, beneficial-owner and banking filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Name Reservation System via cipc.co.za
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a free availability search using the CIPC online name reservation tool. Submit Form CoR 9.5 through CIPC E-Filing with two proposed names and pay the prescribed fee. The reservation is valid for six months and is converted to the company name at incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certified identity or passport copies of the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected or opposed, file Form CoR 9.6 objection or submit an alternative name within 5 business days of the CIPC response.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators, founding directors and CIPC E-Filing delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation and the Notice of Incorporation. Obtain written consents from each initial director and a board/shareholder resolution adopting the registered office and initial share subscriptions. Execute all documents by hand or with an advanced electronic signature under the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 25 of 2002 and initial each page for authenticity.
required_dossiers: Written consent to act as a director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where a document is incomplete or defective, amend and re-execute within 10 business days. If CIPC raises a verification question, provide notarially certified copies of identity documents and resolutions within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Filing to CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to CIPC E-Filing, select 'Company Registration', upload the executed Notice of Incorporation, Memorandum of Incorporation, directors' written consents and name reservation certificate. Electronically pay the prescribed registration fee. Submit the filing and monitor the status under the 'Recent Transactions' panel until a final CIPC decision is issued.
required_dossiers: Executed Form CoR 15.1 Notice of Incorporation
Executed Form CoR 15.1A Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC returns the application with a query, cure the stated deficiency and resubmit within 10 business days. A rejection may be appealed under s. 14 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 through the CIPC appeal process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, CIPC issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and assigns the company registration number. The company is entered into the official Companies Register and becomes a legal personality with limited liability from the date and time, if any, stated in the certificate.
required_dossiers: No additional documentation required for certificate issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated within 30 days of approval, lodge a status escalation through the CIPC Contact Centre and retain proof of filing for any formal engagement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Banking and Beneficial Ownership Post-Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) E-Filing and CIPC E-Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for Income Tax and, if applicable, VAT and PAYE through SARS E-Filing. File the CIPC Beneficial Ownership Declaration identifying all natural persons who ultimately hold or control the company. Open a corporate bank account using the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum of Incorporation and directors' details. Maintain statutory records at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS identifies discrepancies, file corrected tax registration forms with supporting evidence within 30 days. For CIPC beneficial ownership queries, respond through the CIPC query management portal within 14 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no physical industrial footprint; the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition monitors e-commerce consumer protection matters only.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None - automated dropshipping through online networks is not a licensable operational activity under South African law; no retail business licence or manufacturing permit is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical installation, no construction, no industrial emissions; no EIA registration or screening report is mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero on-site wastewater or VOC emissions as the business operates as a virtual intermediary. Any imported goods that require extended producer responsibility under s. 18 of the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008 must be registered with authorized producer responsibility organisations. Standard municipal waste collection applies to office-related waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a home-office or virtual-only operation. If a physical office is later established, the local fire authority must issue a Fire Safety Compliance Certificate and the local municipality an Occupancy/Certificate of Use in accordance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 and municipal zoning bylaws.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — official portal: www.sars.gov.za and SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity carrying on business in South Africa must apply for income tax registration and SARS VAT vendor registration (if taxable supplies exceed the compulsory threshold). Application may be made through SARS eFiling or at a SARS branch. Required documents include the entity's certificate of incorporation, memorandum of incorporation, directors' identification proof, proof of registered address and local business address, bank account details, and powers of attorney for tax representatives. VAT registration requires completion of VAT 101 form, proof of enterprise activities in South Africa, and projected turnover. SARS will issue a taxpayer reference number and a VAT registration number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — South African incorporated companies are tax resident and subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income; non-resident branches are subject to tax on South African source income. No territorial exemption for foreign active business income. Not classified as a pass-through entity. Not located in a designated tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or entity classification election is available under South African law. The Income Tax Act provides certain elections relevant to controlled foreign company (CFC) rules, including the high-tax exemption election under section 9D(2A), the election to defer inclusion of attributable CFC income, and the election to use the transaction price market value basis under transfer pricing rules. Hybrid mismatch elections pursuant to regulations under section 9D are limited and require prescribed documentation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration threshold: ZAR 1,000,000 of taxable supplies in any 12 consecutive months; voluntary registration threshold: ZAR 50,000 of taxable supplies in any 12 consecutive months. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services must register if the aggregate value of electronic services supplied to South African customers exceeds ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping for VAT invoicing. VAT invoices must comply with section 20 of the VAT Act, containing the supplier's name, VAT number, invoice serial number, date, description of goods/services, consideration and tax amount. SARS eFiling requires upload of VAT201 returns and supporting data; no mandatory API-based continuous transaction control clearance. The SARS Tax Administration System does not require pre-clearance of individual invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods are zero-rated where the goods are supplied to a non-resident and are exported from South Africa within 90 days (or such longer period as SARS permits) of the supplier's invoice; the supplier must retain evidence of physical export. Services are zero-rated if supplied to a non-resident and the services are physically rendered outside South Africa, or where the services are supplied to a non-resident in respect of movable property situated outside South Africa. Dropshipping goods directly from foreign suppliers to foreign customers may qualify as zero-rated if the supplier is a mere intermediary and title passes offshore.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 / SARS Customs Clearance Certificate) with customs clearance number
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or equivalent transport document evidencing physical movement of goods from South Africa to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank forex receipt proving foreign currency settlement for the exported goods
Proof of foreign customer's non-resident status (e.g., registered business address abroad)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may disregard zero-rating and assess VAT at the standard rate (15%) if export documentation is incomplete, contradictory, or fraudulent. Additional tax may be imposed under section 89q of the Income Tax Act? Under the Tax Administration Act, an understatement penalty of up to 100% of the shortfall can apply for intentional tax evasion or gross negligence. Criminal prosecution for fraud under the Tax Administration Act and the Customs and Excise Act can lead to imprisonment up to 10 years, and SARS may invoke a full retrospective clawback for all prior export zero-ratings without valid export evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), is the statutory exchange-control authority under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961. Banking prudential oversight is exercised by the SARB Prudential Authority; the national payment system is governed by the National Payment System Act, 1998, with the South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) system serving as the large-value real-time gross settlement rail and the Automated Clearing Bureau (ACB) handling domestic retail ZAR clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The rand (ZAR) is a managed-float, fully convertible currency for bona fide current-account transactions, including dropshipping revenue, import settlements, and cross-border services. Capital-account transactions remain subject to Authorized Dealer reporting and, for specified outflows, FinSurv prior approval. Non-resident direct equity investment is freely permitted without prior SARS or FinSurv sanction, provided the inward funds are routed through an Authorized Dealer, recorded under the inward direct-investment purpose classification, and evidenced in the dealer's exchange-control records so that future dividend and capital repatriation via Form A2 is legally protected. Profit remittance is permitted once profits are declared, dividends tax at 20% (or a reduced treaty rate evidenced by a SARS withholding-tax certificate) is settled, and standard banking documentation is submitted. There are no hard convertibility quotas on the corporate sector, but exchange-control penalties apply to unreported foreign receivables and offshore retention of export proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to South Africa through the exporter's Authorized Dealer within 180 days of the shipment date; extensions may be requested from FinSurv through the dealer upon proof of justified delay, such as extended supplier credit terms or disputed receivables. There is no fixed statutory percentage conversion ratio: proceeds may either be converted to ZAR at the prevailing interbank rate or retained in a permitted Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held at an Authorized Dealer. However, every receipt must be routed through the named dealer and supported by shipping and order documentation. For automated dropshipping, each PayPal/Stripe payout batch must be mapped to order-level export evidence (customer, SKU, price, tracked consignment, commercial invoice) to satisfy the 180-day rule and FICA record-keeping; failure to repatriate or leaving funds on an offshore EMI/PSP balance is an exchange-control offence subject to criminal sanctions and administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined Annual Return (CAR): annual return, beneficial ownership confirmation and Financial Accountability Supplement (prescribed fee approximately ZAR 650)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; the CAR regime applies to annual returns due on or after 1 May 2025
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of the annual-return fee for each commenced month of delay, capped at 100% of the prescribed fee; company flagged 'In Default'; failure to file for two consecutive anniversary periods exposes the company to CIPC deregistration/strike-off under s 82(3)(b) Companies Act 71 of 2008

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: ITR14 annual corporate income tax return (year of assessment return of income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year; SARS eFiling season deadline per tax year applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS administrative penalty under ss 210-213 Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011: fixed monthly penalty up to ZAR 8,500, or a percentage penalty of 10% of assessed tax for higher-income entities; understatement penalty up to 200% under s 223 TAA; daily interest on unpaid tax; SARS may raise a default assessment and institute criminal proceedings for persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provisional tax (IRD6): first, second and optional third (top-up) provisional estimates and payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First provisional within 6 months of commencement of the year of assessment; second provisional on the last business day of the year of assessment; third/top-up provisional within 6 months after the end of the year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% penalty on the shortfall where the estimate is less than the actual liability by more than the greater of 10% of actual liability or ZAR 20,000 (s 162 TAA); interest at the prescribed SARS rate accrues on late payments

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (normal corporate tax rate for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday exists in South Africa. Available relief includes the Small Business Corporation (SBC) graduated rate schedule (0% up to ZAR 95,000 taxable income; 7% and 21% in the middle bands; 27% above ZAR 550,000 for qualifying 2024/25 years), s12E accelerated capital allowances, s11D research and development enhanced deductions, s12H learnership allowances, and ordinary s11(a) trading expense deductions for e-commerce costs such as software, fulfilment, courier, payment gateway and advertising expenses.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory expiry for companies under s20 of the Income Tax Act, 1962; assessed losses may be carried forward indefinitely while the trade continues, but are extinguished if the company permanently ceases trading.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 — Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through the SARS eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year (year of assessment). A (Pty) Ltd with a 31 March year-end must therefore file by the following 31 March; SARS may issue a default assessment under s95 of the Tax Administration Act where a return is not delivered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross receipts from dropshipping sales, including product sale proceeds, customer shipping fees, settlement adjustments, commissions and ancillary revenue received in cash, card and online payment methods, before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert foreign currency (USD, EUR, GBP) into ZAR using the SARS spot exchange rate on the date of settlement; report all Stripe and PayPal settlements irrespective of payment-gateway chargebacks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local dividends exempt under s10(1)(k)(i), foreign dividends qualifying for the participation exemption under s10B(3), and other statutorily exempt receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document foreign dividend exemption conditions (minimum 10% shareholding in foreign company and no CFC hybrid claims) to avoid aggressive SARS audit adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Maritime costs directly attributable to the dropshipping trade: cost of inventory sold, freight and courier charges, payment-processing fees, platform subscription fees, website hosting, cloud software, marketing, and bad debts incurred in the production of income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany payments to foreign suppliers and IP licensors must be arm's-length and supported by contemporaneous transfer-pricing notes; SARS may disallow deductions for unsubstantiated related-party flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year assessed losses, where the same trade has been carried on, available to offset taxable income in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned dormant shell that did not trade in the prior loss year cannot apply the assessed loss until the trade recommences and records demonstrate continuous trade.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 — Taxable income before assessed loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income determined after all deductions and exemptions and before applying the brought-forward assessed loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the base against which the 27% normal corporate tax is calculated before any SBC graduated-rate concession.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 — Normal tax at corporate rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Normal tax computed at 27% (or the applicable SBC graduated rate) on taxable income, less any applicable payments already made through provisional tax (IRP6).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Shareholders domiciled abroad are not entitled to a company rebate; ensure foreign directors do not offset personal taxes against the South African company's corporate tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all cross-border connected-party transactions including purchases from foreign related suppliers, management fees, royalty payments, interest on shareholder loans, and automated fulfilment services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the SARS transfer-pricing schedule with a functional and risk analysis; failure to disclose connected-party transactions in the ITR14 may trigger s31 TP audits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of distributions declared during the year, the gross amount of dividends paid, and the dividends tax withheld at 20%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach DTR01/DTR02 declarations and the shareholder's tax residency certificate (TRC) before claiming any treaty-reduced dividend withholding rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to submit the ITR14 triggers an administrative non-compliance penalty under s210/s211 of the Tax Administration Act of ZAR 250 per month for small taxpayers up to ZAR 16,000 per month for large enterprises; unpaid normal tax attracts interest at the SARS prescribed rate (currently repo rate plus 3.5% per annum). A substantial or deliberate understatement may expose the company to understatement penalties of 25% to 125% of the shortfall, and criminal tax evasion may result in a fine up to ZAR 10 million and imprisonment up to five years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 — Provisional Company Tax Return; submitted via SARS eFiling as an interim payment declaration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Periodic (two or three provisional tax payments per year of assessment; not an annual return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First provisional payment: on or before the last day of the sixth month after the start of the financial year. Second provisional payment: on or before the last day of the financial year. Optional third voluntary top-up payment: within six months after the financial year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimate of current-year taxable income before applying assessed losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign directors must base the estimate on actual six-month results and avoid underestimating to circumvent provisional tax interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 27% of estimated taxable income (or SBC graduated rate), reduced by any applicable rebates or credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No deduction in the estimate is permitted for foreign income taxes paid by non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total of prior provisional payments made during the year of assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain IRP6 accepting-for-payment records available for SARS inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance payable or overpayment to be carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A refund may be withheld if the company's underlying bank account does not match the SARS registration profile; maintain local banking substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-submission of IRP6 exposes the company to administrative penalties under s210 TAA (ZAR 250 to ZAR 8,000 per month) plus interest at the prescribed rate. Underestimation with a low-credit estimate can trigger a 20% underestimation penalty under the Fourth Schedule if the estimate turns out to be less than 80% of the actual taxable income.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% Dividends Tax on the amount of any dividend (cash, in specie, or deemed dividend) paid by a South African resident company to shareholders, payable to SARS by the end of the month following the dividend distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Dividend tax treaty relief is not automatic. The non-resident beneficial owner must submit a duly completed DTR01 (Declaration by Beneficial Owner of Dividend for purposes of an Approved Double Taxation Agreement), DTR02 (Notification by the Paying Entity), and a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home tax jurisdiction. The South African paying company must retain these documents before declaring the dividend, and must apply the reduced treaty rate (typically 0%, 5% or 15% depending on the DTA, shareholding percentage and shareholder type). If documentation is incomplete, the full 20% must be withheld and remitted to SARS, and the non-resident can subsequently claim a refund only via SARS assessment or a DTA mutual agreement procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid by a South African company to a non-resident is generally subject to a 15% statutory withholding tax on interest, reduced by certain DTA rates to 0% or 10%, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and a valid TRC and WHT declaration are submitted. Royalties or IP licence fees paid to a non-resident (e.g., e-commerce software, proprietary dropshipping algorithms, trademarks) are subject to a final 15% royalty withholding tax under s49B; most South African DTAs reduce the statutory rate to 10% or 12%, but denial of relief applies where the connected-party arrangements lack economic substance. Both charges must be accounted for on the SARS WHTI/WHTR returns and paid within the prescribed month-end deadline.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: South African law does not provide a statutory de minimis threshold for Local File or Master File preparation. The Country-by-Country Report threshold is ZAR 10 billion consolidated annual group revenue for MNE groups. SARS expects contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation for every material cross-border connected transaction; in practice, disclosure of cross-border related-party transactions on the ITR14 transfer-pricing schedule is monitored at an annual transactional value of ZAR 5 million or more. Taxpayers should prepare a Local File to justify arm's-length pricing for any transaction with a non-resident connected person, regardless of size, and be able to produce it within 30 days of a SARS request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to the UAE. However, the general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) in s80A–s80L, s103 of the Income Tax Act, controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution in s9D, and the OECD-aligned transfer-pricing doctrine require the local (Pty) Ltd to demonstrate commercial substance – including local board decision-making, personnel, premises, bank accounts, contractual risk and actual risk assumption. A drop-shipping company that is tax-resident in South Africa but functions as a bare pass-through with no local economic activity and no risk exposure is vulnerable to being recharacterised as a limited-risk distributor, leading to upward profit adjustments, deemed-dividend treatment, and denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting dropshipping turnover derived from Stripe or PayPal settlements, understating sales, fabricating supplier invoices, using nominee bank accounts, or backdating the winding-up to conceal taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty of 25% to 125% of the shortfall under s222 of the Tax Administration Act; criminal prosecution under s234 TAA with a fine of up to ZAR 10 million per count and imprisonment for up to five years; interest at the prescribed rate runs on the unpaid taxes without interruption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false ITR14s or authorise diversion of revenue are personally liable as 'persons who knowingly permit a false return' under s235 TAA; SARS may obtain a civil restraint order or travel ban, and imprisonment is a standard outcome in fraudulent revenue-diversion cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematically pricing dropshipping product purchases, management fees, IP licences, or marketing payments to a foreign connected party at an excessive level so the South African company reports little or no taxable income; failing to prepare contemporaneous TP documentation or filing false OECD declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS has power to adjust the taxable income under s31 of the Income Tax Act, impose a secondary deemed-dividend adjustment, apply understatement penalties up to 125%, and impose administrative fines per non-compliant ITR14 schedule. Interest on the additional assessment is mandatory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who caused the company to transfer profits offshore without arm's-length justification can be jointly and severally liable for the additional tax under common law breach of fiduciary duty; criminal tax investigations may disqualify directors and prohibit travel while money-laundering charges are assessed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Corporation / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominally incorporated South African (Pty) Ltd with no local employees, no office, no board meetings, no operating bank account, and no trading records, purely to avoid foreign tax or to launder online dropshipping sales through Stripe and PayPal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS and the Companies Tribunal can reject the corporate form as a sham under substance-over-form doctrine, disallow all deductions, and treat the income as accruing to the real foreign beneficial owner under s7(2)-(4) of the Income Tax Act; failure to maintain registered address and annual returns leads to automatic deregistration under the Companies Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Depositing commercial receipts into a director's personal account triggers statutory personal liability under s20(9) of the Companies Act and s172/s179 of the Tax Administration Act, enabling garnishee orders, attachment of foreign assets, travel bans and director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a high-volume, automated dropshipping payment flow through Stripe/PayPal without FICA-compliant identity verification (KYC), beneficial ownership controls, transaction monitoring, or suspicious transaction reporting; providing false beneficial ownership information to payment processors or banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 38 of 2001, administrative penalties of up to ZAR 10 million may be imposed on accountable institutions for each contravention; criminal sanctions for serious, wilful non-compliance reach 15 years' imprisonment and asset forfeiture. Payment processors and banks are independently required to terminate the account and report to the Financial Intelligence Centre.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who enable AML breaches with knowledge enjoy no corporate shield; personal liability, criminal prosecution, travel bans and freezing orders are routinely applied to beneficial owners of online payment infrastructures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Dividends, Interest and Royalty Taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring a dividend to a foreign parent or non-resident shareholder without deducting the 20% Dividends Tax, paying interest on a cross-border shareholder loan without 15% interest WHT, or paying IP royalties to a foreign licensor without remitting the 15% royalty WHT and without obtaining a TRC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company remains liable as withholding agent for the full tax amount not withheld, plus a 10% late-payment penalty and interest at the prescribed rate; SARS may also impose administrative non-compliance penalties and deny the deduction for the underlying royalty or interest if the WHT is unpaid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise a distribution or cross-border payment knowing that withholding tax has not been remitted are personally liable under s235 of the Tax Administration Act and the Fourth Schedule; civil recovery plus travel restrictions and criminal conviction can follow.
